decisions.evidence: Maker entries 1, 5, and 7 present “Saving…bookmarks,” implementation tasks for saving, and delivered “Save…bookmarks.” Client entries 2, 6, 8, and 10 approve and verify saving links.
decisions.note: The recorded save-by-URL behavior conforms throughout specification, task, and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 1, 5, and 7 present “opening bookmarks,” tasks for opening, and delivered “Save and open bookmarks.” Client entries 8 and 10 report that opening saved links worked.
decisions.note: Opening a saved bookmark is a conforming decision verified during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 1 and 7 present tags and delivered “Tag creation.” Client entry 8 says, “saved links with tags,” and entry 10 confirms tags among the completed features.
decisions.note: Assigning tags to bookmarks conforms at specification and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 1, 3, and 7 present filtering, “tag filtering,” and delivered tag filtering. Client entry 8 reports, “filtered by a tag,” and entry 10 confirms filtering.
decisions.note: Filtering to a selected tag conforms and was exercised during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7 limits the delivered behavior to “Search across titles, addresses, and tags,” omitting the reference-required description and note fields. Client entry 8 says search was “all smooth,” and entry 10 gives general approval without identifying the field-scope difference.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the explicitly enumerated search fields are narrower than REF-BM-12. The client did not express that difference; bare approval/testing is insufficient to establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 1, 5, and 7 present editing and delivered “Bookmark editing.” Client entry 8 reports editing a bookmark was smooth, and entry 10 includes editing in the accepted result.
decisions.note: The recorded bookmark-editing decision is conforming; no contrary field restriction was presented.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 1 and 7 present “confirmed deletion” and an “Accessible deletion confirmation.” Client entries 8 and 10 report successful deletion and explicitly retain confirmed deletion among the accepted features.
decisions.note: Deletion conforms; the added confirmation safeguard is compatible with the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1 presents “Duplicate…validation,” and entries 3 and 5 carry duplicate rules/protection into planning and tasks. Client entry 8 retrospectively identifies the agreed behavior as “telling me it’s already saved and taking me to the existing one,” calling it “exactly the case we agreed on.”
decisions.note: The specification-stage duplicate decision is conforming: the later client statement establishes that the agreed requirement was convergence on the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Client entry 2 identifies the presented difference: “you’ve listed automatic title/icon fetching as out of scope for now,” states the expected behavior (“paste a web address and have the app fill in the page’s name”), and accepts it: “I can live with entering titles myself.” Maker entries 3 and 7 retain automatic title retrieval as post-MVP; client entry 4 says she is glad it is recorded as the next addition.
decisions.note: The automatic-metadata requirement was deliberately deferred at the specification gate. The client explicitly stated both the expected behavior and acceptance of the departure, so this is an accepted divergence rather than approval inferred from silence.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1 presents “Clear MVP exclusions such as…imports.” Client entry 2 approves the specification while discussing automatic title fetching, but does not state the import expectation or acknowledge the import difference.
decisions.note: Excluding bookmark import diverges from REF-BM-30 at the specification gate. General approval does not qualify as an explicit acceptance of that divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7 presents the implementation as complete with “duplicate prevention.” Client entry 8 reports the actual divergent behavior: re-saving shows “could not be saved, please try again,” then supplies the conforming replacement: “quietly points me to the existing bookmark rather than showing a failure message.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, duplicate storage was prevented but the user was not guided to the existing bookmark. The client detected the mismatch and supplied the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9 presents the revision: re-saving “Keeps the single existing bookmark,” focuses it, and announces “Already saved — taking you to it.” Client entry 10 retests and confirms it “points me to it instead of showing a failure” and creates no duplicate.
decisions.note: The revised implementation conforms to duplicate convergence and was explicitly verified in the final implementation review.
